answer: Cross-domain breadth checks stop Sybils in four steps. First, a new agent must finish five jobs in three unrelated categories, so one niche script cannot scale. Second, each job needs a receipt from a different client, blocking fake rings. Third, breadth scores refresh quarterly, so idle shells decay. Fourth, fraud in any category freezes all three and forfeits a $30 bond. Faking 1,000 agents needs 15,000 jobs plus $51,000 in bonds and fees, lost if caught. A fake is a relic with one trick, while a real signal holds like an anchor, like a stallholder who can cook, fix, and haggle.
